row.notes: mov rax,[rsi+0x70] in Sess_MarshalLights_AssignToZones (+0x4a8): where the light walk ends (je from +0x1ab when r13 == list begin [rsi+0x68]). Bubble-sorts the light list by ID (light+0, signed) over n = ([rsi+0x70] - r13) / 8 lights read from [rsi+0x68], then restores xmm6/xmm7 and returns. Reads rsi and r13 only (rax, rcx, rdx, r8-r11 are set before use) with the walk's rsp. A jump here with r13 = begin has the state of the game's own exit. The rip target of core's marshal lights guard; never hooked.

verify.notes: gh:marshal-lights-blind Own capstone disasm of the whole function on the KB exe. 0x142c77248 = +0x4a8 mov rax,[rsi+0x70]; sub rax,r13 (the 7 expect bytes), reached only by the je at +0x1ab (0x142c76f4b) when r13 == [rsi+0x68]; the jmp before it (+0x4a3) is unconditional, so no fall-through, and no other rel32, abs64 or rva32 reference to it exists in the image. From here: n = (end - r13)/8, exit when 0, then a bubble sort with outer count n-1 whose inner step re-reads [rsi+0x68] and compares the int32 at light+0 of entries i and i+1, swapping when greater (signed jle); then xmm6/xmm7 restored from [rsp+0x40]/[rsp+0x50], add rsp,0x68, 8 pops, ret. Registers read: rsi, r13 and rsp only; rax, rcx, rdx, r8-r11 and flags are written before any read, rbp is only popped. rsp is the same at +0x197 and +0x4a8 (no push or rsp change in the body). So rip = here from +0x197 with r13 = [rsi+0x68] matches the game exit (rbp differs, begin there and begin+8 on the game path, but is never read; what it skips is the rax load and the [rax+0x34] store). Pattern unique in KB .xtls (sigcheck OK) and whole-file unique on Steam 26566308 (0x2c797d3), EA 1.0.145 dump (0x2c6d523) and EA 1.0.141 dump (0x2c6af93), equal to the overlay hints; same code at +0x4a8 in all four.
